newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close easier on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close easier on profit-taking.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended lower in brisk trading on Tuesday as investors took profits after recent gains.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 23.34 points to close at 6249.24.
Trading was brisk at 107.8 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion).
Maison Placements Canada President John Ing said market players took the opportunity to unload some holdings after Toronto's 150-point gain over the previous three sessions.
Investors are awaiting more U.S. economic data this week for possible signs of inflation and an indication of whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike short-term interest rates at a May 20 meeting.
April's producer price index will be released on Wednesday. Economists expect it to be unchanged after slipping 0.1 percent in March.
Most of Toronto's 14 sub-indices dipped, led by golds, conglomerates and consumer products. The four gaining sectors were media, real estate, retail and oils.
Declining issues edged out advancers 492 to 484, while 321 traded flat.
In individual issues, Gandalf Technologies Inc. jumped C$2.08 to C$3.48 amid rumors that the computer networking firm may have secured U.S. financing or even a partner, analysts said.
Ottawa-based Gandalf said it knew of no corporate development that could explain the activity.
Gandalf, which has been unprofitable during its implementation of a new sales distribution system, will release fourth-quarter earnings on Wednesday.

Gold prospector Corriente Resources Inc. tumbled C$3.75 to C$6.40 on drilling results from a southern Peru project that showed "widespread but low-grade gold mineralization." Corriente Vice President Henk van Alphen called the results "unfortunate."
